about: Every factual sentence the site states about Yantrik OS, with the file in the OS repository that establishes it. Rendered by the Claim component, so the words and their source cannot drift apart; checked by scripts/check-claims.mjs at build (the source must exist at the pinned commit, and the check must be under 60 days old).

claims.text: Sixteen apps ship. ySheets and Music are shelved, and the shell says why.
Eighteen app surfaces and five service surfaces publish what they hold and what they can be asked to do.
claims.limit: Regenerated from the code on every build.

claims.text: Every action is graded safe, standard, sensitive or dangerous. The machine has a ceiling nothing passes, in any mode.
The mode decides what runs unasked: plan, ask, auto, or a time-boxed bypass with a countdown on the status bar.
claims.limit: Bypass is never saved across a restart.

claims.text: Five minds attach over one socket today: Yantrik Mind, Hermes, Pi, DeepSeek and OpenClaw.
claims.limit: None starts until it is configured.

claims.text: Claude, Codex and Gemini accounts are shown and switched in the Minds panel; sign-in happens in the vendor's own program, and the desktop holds no credential.
claims.limit: They are accounts, not minds that attach.

claims.text: The harness protocol is seven methods, with no field for an endpoint, a model or a key.
An approval card names the caller twice: what it says it is, and what the kernel says it is. The grade comes from the app, not the caller.
A grant is single-use, bound to the exact arguments, and given only by a person's pointer.
Once a session has read something private, it will not type into a page or open an address that could carry it out. No tool clears that, and bypass does not switch it off.
The vault is AES-256-GCM, with its key wrapped under Argon2id once a passphrase exists.
claims.limit: On the live image and autologin installs it is not wrapped, and the desktop says so.

claims.text: A forward proxy sees only host names and starts in audit.
claims.limit: The default-deny wall is a switch the person turns; it is not on by default.

claims.text: Private mode refuses agents on every door and freezes the person's agents.
claims.limit: A harness started by hand outside the desktop's units is not frozen.

claims.text: An agent cannot read the person's own conversation; it reads its own session.
Apps a mind opens go to Mind View, a desktop of its own in one window.
claims.limit: If Mind View cannot start, the app opens on your desktop and the shell says why.

claims.text: Settings lists free AI tiers, one account per provider. A key goes from the clipboard to the vault and never reaches a model; providers that may train on prompts are marked and never get a private turn.
claims.limit: Free tiers change often; the list says when it was last checked.

claims.text: Provider sign-up and key pages open in a separate browser with no remote-debugging port.
Memory is YantrikDB: SQLite with vector search, a knowledge graph and an encrypted vault, kept in /opt/yantrik/data.
Updates verify the bundle's checksum, keep a backup, and roll back if the shell does not answer.
claims.limit: Nightly is the only published channel; manifests are not yet signed.

claims.text: Every published image is boot-tested in QEMU.
claims.limit: Real hardware and UEFI are untested.

claims.text: The whole desktop uses about 186 MB of memory.
The live machine is a sealed virtual machine behind a gate that holds the stream's secrets. The page is view-only, at three frames a second.
claims.limit: What the mind is doing, its model and its uptime are not published by the machine yet.

claims.text: The OS sends nothing on its own; the update check and a problem report you send are the exceptions.
claims.limit: Applications are not sandboxed: software you install runs with your own access.

claims.text: Fifty skills ship as plain YAML.
The live machine streams its 1280×800 screen at three frames a second, with no audio.
claims.limit: Size and rate read off the stream with ffprobe on 1 Oct 2026.

claims.text: Its video goes to a gate on a sealed network segment that has no path in from the LAN. The relay’s secrets are kept on the gate, so nothing on the machine, its mind included, has them to show.
The relay takes one publisher on one path and serves the stream read-only, through this site’s own server. Everything else it could serve is switched off.
The live page plays the stream only while frames are arriving. Twenty seconds without a new frame is offline, said in words, never a frozen picture.
Yantrik OS ships as a Debian 13 (trixie) live ISO for x86-64. There is no ARM build and no 32-bit build.
Only the nightly channel has builds. Beta and stable are names the updater knows; nothing has been published to either.
install.sh prints the current image’s address, size and sha256, and stops. Only with --download does it write a file, and it refuses the file if the sha256 does not match.
The image ships no language model and no mind. You point it at one in first-run setup.
Known to work: QEMU/KVM with 4 vCPU, 8 GB of RAM, a 32 GB disk, no GPU and BIOS firmware, the project’s own test machine. CI boots every image with 4 GB and 4 CPUs.
claims.limit: Below 4 GB of RAM is not measured.

claims.text: Not measured: real hardware of any kind, the UEFI boot path, any GPU but QEMU’s virtio-vga, Wi-Fi on real adapters, and VirtualBox.
The disk installer erases the disk you give it, needs one of at least 6 GB, and has not been through the boot test the image has.
On the live image the user is yantrik with the password yantrik and passwordless sudo. SSH is installed and turned off.
The status bar names the mind that is answering, and whether it is local or cloud.
In ask, the default, a sensitive or dangerous action puts a card in front of you. Auto asks only about dangerous ones. Plan refuses every change.
The grade belongs to the action and is set in the app’s own code: in Notes, opening a note is standard and exporting one to a file is sensitive.
